newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHT - CORPORATEFAMILY UP 30 PCT.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHT - CORPORATEFAMILY UP 30 PCT.

text.p: Shares of CorporateFamily Solutions Inc surged more than 30 percent as Wall Street gave a warm welcome to the company's Wall Street debut.
CorporateFamily, which provides child care at workplace sites, rose to 13 in afternoon trading from its $10 a share initial public offering price. Earlier the stock was as high as 13-1/2.

A total of 2.35 million shares were sold in the IPO, with one million by selling shareholders and 1.35 million by the company. Montgomery Securities and J.C. Bradford & Co were the managing underwriters of the offering.
The company raised roughly $13.5 million in the IPO, with enough demand to price at the very high end of expectations of $8-$10 a share.

The Nashville, Tennessee company says its mission is to help clients create a "family friendly" workplace, operating kindergartens, summer camps, and child care services at or near the offices of its clients.
With a growing number of families with two working parents, more and more companies are trying to help employees meet their family responsibilities, according to its prospectus.
Its impressive client list includes AlliedSignal Inc, Boeing Co, Chase Manhattan Corp and other Fortune 500 companies.

CorporateFamily was founded by a diverse bunch: president and chief executive Marguerite Sallee; Lamar Alexander, a former presidential candidate, U.S. Secretary of Education and Governor of Tennessee; Bob Keeshan (television's "Captain Kangaroo"); former vice chairman of the Corporation for Public Broadcasting Honey Alexander; and Proffitt's Inc chairman and chief executive of Brad Martin.
The company manages 87 centers for 65 clients in 27 states, and has 17 centers undcer development.
